title: Steward handoff and off-ramp play notes (WIP)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working-notes doc for the rollout steward handoff + off-ramp choreography used across Console-driven heterogeneous experiments (hosted + dedicated). Goal: a compact, actionable checklist and decision lattice that a steward can use during a shift handoff or when executing an off-ramp (fast rollback, traffic quarantine, staged reversion). Keep this intentionally terse — references and runbooks linked rather than duplicated.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Who: rollout steward (ops/product/eng rotation)
- What: transfer ownership, validate signal baselines, enforce off-ramp thresholds, and coordinate remediation if gates trip
- When: pre-launch, during first 48h of exposure, and any high-sensitivity window (e.g., regulatory cohorts)

Before the handoff (pre-shift checklist):
- Notification: steward-to-steward Slack ping in #rollout-stewards with: brief status, current exposure %, known risks, primary metrics. Template: "STEW-START: feature X, exposure 3%, model v14 -> v15 split, primary signals: latency P95, cost/sec, top-3 safety rejects. On-call: eng: @ethan, product: @maya. Link: <console/experiment/987>"
- Snapshot: take a telemetry snapshot (last 6h) and upload to the handoff thread. Include: token-rate, P50/P95 latency, per-route error-rate, accept-rate (successful responses), regression% on eval prompt set.
- Warm test: run 12 synthetic queries through the same routing policy (record responses, latency, KV cache warm hit %). Attach JSON responses.
- Known mitigations: list of active fallbacks (soft-fallback route, lower-capacity region, model-variant fallback) and how to trigger them (Console toggle path + API call examples).

Handoff script (during shift swap, 3–5 min):
1) Read quick TL;DR aloud in handoff voice channel.
2) Share link to active runbook and the most recent snapshot.
3) Walk the incoming steward through: what to watch, how to read the signal dashboard, and where escalation lives (Slack fold, PagerDuty runbook).
4) Confirm escalation contacts and ownership for remediation tasks (who cuts traffic, who merges revert PR, who patches routing policies).

Primary signals to monitor (baseline + escalation thresholds):
- Latency: P95 > baseline * 1.3 -> start investigation; P95 > baseline * 1.5 for 10m -> off-ramp candidate.
- Error rate: client-4xx + server-5xx combined increase of +0.5 percentage points absolute AND relative increase > 50% over baseline -> deeper triage.
- Quality regressions: automated eval drift (weighted score) drop by 3+ points vs. baseline on guard-set -> pause exposure and human review.
- Safety moderation: content-moderation flags > baseline + 2x or sudden spike in category-specific flags (e.g., hallucination-related heuristics) -> immediate quarantine.
- Cost velocity: spend per minute > expected * 2 for sustained 5m -> investigate batching / model size mismatch.

Off-ramp decision flow (fast checklist):
- Step 0: quick confirm (2 min) that telemetry artifacts are real (not dashboard anomaly). Run the quick SQL checks (queries below) or hit the observability API.
- Step 1: if latency or error thresholds breached, reduce exposure to 25% of current (Console traffic slider) and re-evaluate for 10m.
- Step 2: if issue persists, toggle soft-fallback route to previous model-variant (Console -> routing -> fallback). Notify stakeholders.
- Step 3: if quality drift or safety spike triggered, immediate 100% off-ramp (full revert or model removal). Start incident channel and capture sample responses for forensics.
- Step 4: follow up with post-incident signal review and commit to fixes before re-expansion.

Quick observability queries (placeholders to paste into the observability query runner):
- Token rate / minute: SELECT minute, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE experiment_id=987 GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 60;
- Error delta: SELECT status_code, count(*) FROM requests WHERE experiment_id=987 AND ts > now()-interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY status_code;
- Quality sample: SELECT request_id, prompt_hash, response_snippet FROM evaluations WHERE experiment_id=987 AND label IN ('bad','edge') ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;
- Model routing breakdown: SELECT route, count(*) FROM requests WHERE experiment_id=987 GROUP BY route;

Steward rotation and coverage notes:
- Shift length: prefer 4–6h steward blocks for first 72h of exposure. Overlap 10 minutes between handoffs.
- Primary vs backup: always have a designated backup for the first 24h. Backup should be able to reduce traffic and toggle fallbacks.
- Escalation practice: if top-tier signals trip, pager to eng-sre (escalation list in linked runbook).

Communication artifacts (templates):
- Slack snippet for partial rollback: "ACTION: reduced exposure to 25% for feature X due to increased P95. Steward: @maya. Investigation in #rollout-987. If you're affected, please surface sample requests."
- Incident-start message: "INCIDENT: model v15 showed quality regression on guard-set. Off-ramped to v14 at 14:12 PST. Creating incident channel: #inc-987. Triage: @ethan (eng), @sofia (prod), @jun (sre)."

Simulation / rehearsal recipe (weekly cadence):
- Playbook: run a synthetic latency spike and safety-flag increase by injecting test traffic into a staging experiment. Verify steward can perform the off-ramp steps within 5 minutes.
- Post-simulation checklist: time-to-offramp, missed signals, communication lag. Log lessons in this doc.

Open questions / WIP items:
- How to automatically correlate model-variant weight changes to per-cohort latency (need a small telemetry project ticket).
- Should we add a secondary lightweight quality check on-signal that runs 1% of requests through a fast eval? (pro/con notes below)
- Ownership map for cross-region fallbacks: confirm who will accept the regulatory trade-offs for region-specific off-ramps.

Notes for integration with Console features:
- Expose a one-click steward handoff snapshot export (dashboard -> export snapshot -> slack thread) is high value. Filing GH issue above.
- Need: traffic slider API idempotency guarantee so two stewards reducing traffic concurrently don't cause flip-flop.

Post-offramp tasks (next 72h):
- Collect a sample of affected requests (min 500 or 24h, whichever smaller) and run the regression eval suite.
- Create a remediation issue with triage notes and owner, link to incident channel.
- Schedule a re-run window with reduced exposure and a steward assigned for the re-introduction.

Appendix: quick decision matrix (one-line)
- latency transient (<10m): monitor
- latency sustained (>10m) or error spike: reduce exposure to 25%
- quality or safety regression: immediate off-ramp, incident channel

References and bookmarks:
- Console rollout API docs (internal): confluence://rollouts/console-api
- Staged rollback examples: GH: redwood-inference/ops-scripts#54
- Experiment telemetry schema: confluence://telemetry/experiment-schema

Last updated notes:
- 2025-01-17: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-02-02: added quick SQL checks and steward overlap guidance (Ethan)

End of notes.
